units.title: The actual independent Gaussian inputs for the first Picard layer
units.boundary: This constructs the first refresh noise and first finite Picard innovation array. The incoming run-wide moment, second array, second refresh, quadrature data, numerical D.7 and D.8 remain separate.

sources.label: Chen–Chewi–Lu–Zhang, Algorithm 3.1
sources.scope: Independent zeta_0 and G_j^[0] draws; Lemma D.4 uses their second moments.

assumptions: The incoming phase-state law is a probability measure with an integrable combined square bounded by M≥0.
The phase length is nonnegative and the Picard index type is finite.
E is a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space.
units.statement: On the nested product of the incoming law, a fresh standard Gaussian, and a finite product of standard Gaussians, the refreshed X and P0 and every Picard innovation G_j are measurable and square-integrable with their exact consumer-ready moment bounds.

steps.title: Build the probability space
steps.text: The nested product measure represents freshness of the first refresh Gaussian and the first Picard innovation array.
steps.lean: Measure.prod constructs the refresh factor and Measure.pi constructs the finite innovation array.

steps.title: Reuse the refresh calculation
steps.text: The previous theorem already proves measurability, integrability, and the corrected OU moment budget; product integration lifts it unchanged over the extra innovation array.
steps.lean: Integrable.comp_fst and integral_prod transport the established result.

steps.title: Read each Gaussian coordinate
steps.text: Evaluation at j is measurable. Finite-product marginal integration returns the original standard Gaussian law, so every coordinate has exactly dimension d as its squared-norm moment.
steps.lean: integrable_comp_eval and integral_comp_eval are the pinned Mathlib APIs.

steps.title: Feed the real variables to the next theorem
steps.text: The focused test passes the product-law coordinate projections to the two-layer Picard moment theorem, and separately checks a nondegenerate one-dimensional Gaussian coordinate moment.
steps.lean: Tests.SmoothedPicardHMCPartialMomentumRefresh checks symbolic API composition in dimension zero and the exact positive-dimensional Gaussian moment in E=R.

units.lean_statement: The nested lets expose the exact probability law and random variables, while the conjunction returns every measurability and integrability premise required downstream.
units.lean_proof: ASTIS owns the OU refresh and Gaussian norm-square results. Mathlib owns finite product measures, coordinate marginals, and product integration.
